name: Proposed stablecoin-issuer AML and sanctions risk-program context

attribution.legal_posture: Official notice of proposed rulemaking using allegation-based risk evidence; it is a proposal, while final rule, adjudicated case, sanctions designation and transaction-level indicator require later action.

caveats: The proposed 2026 financial-sector regulatory framework cites 2025 forfeiture allegations; the case count remains tied to the cited forfeiture matter.
Label this as a proposal and allegations; the rule remains unfinalized, while stablecoin usage alone remains an insufficient basis for suspicion.
This record includes no people, personas, victim institutions, front companies, accounts, wallets, payment identifiers, addresses, or images.
Treat controls as risk-based and source-qualified; DPRK linkage requires multiple corroborated signals.

statements: FinCEN and OFAC cite alleged stablecoin use by DPRK IT workers as one reason payment-stablecoin issuers need risk-based AML and sanctions programs. The defensible publication point is governance and monitoring coverage for payroll-like or contractor-payment channels, not publication of account or wallet indicators.
limitations: Label as a proposal and allegations; do not state that the rule is final or that stablecoin usage alone is suspicious.
The proposed 2026 financial-sector regulatory framework cites 2025 forfeiture allegations; it does not establish another forfeiture case.
Treat controls as risk-based and source-qualified; no single location, language, accent, camera, payment, network, device, or behavioral signal establishes DPRK linkage.
This record includes no people, personas, victim institutions, front companies, accounts, wallets, payment identifiers, addresses, or images.

sources.support: The proposal cites alleged DPRK IT-worker laundering through stablecoins and states that a 2025 forfeiture complaint alleged workers requested stablecoin payment because of value stability and easier conversion to fiat. The example supports proposed AML and sanctions-program obligations for payment-stablecoin issuers.
